neighbours.label: comma or semicolon closing a clause-internal phrase before the sentence continues (this season, | the left and the right,)
fire: If you had told fans they would finish above the champions this season, nobody would have believed you.
Successive governments, both of the left and the right, have ignored the problem.
Anyone who tries to trap or capture an endangered species, or to attempt to do so, faces a fine.
The great machine was built near the docks by a local firm, and it still runs today.
Taxes on fuel, as everyone in the valley knows, have doubled since spring.
The parish records, though badly damaged by water, survived the war.
Our coach, who had played for the club in his youth, resigned in March.
Prices in the old market, unlike those in the mall, stayed low all year.
quiet: Nobody would have believed fans if they had said the team would finish above the champions.
Successive governments from every party have ignored the problem for years.
Anyone who tries to trap or capture an endangered species faces a heavy fine.
The great machine built near the docks by a local firm still runs today.
Everyone in the valley knows that taxes on fuel have doubled since spring.
The badly damaged parish records survived the war in a cellar.
Our coach played for the club in his youth and resigned in March.
Prices in the old market stayed low all year while the mall got dearer.

notes: Top: ',' x9 after 'this season', 'left and the right', 'endangered species'; also a year digit and GUID digit. Low-confidence guess.
